models_evaluated: six LLMs (others not named in abstract)

links.outcome: Hallucination rate under adversarial fabricated inputs, and effect of temperature 0 on reproducibility/errors
links.effect: Hallucination rates ranged 50% to 82%; temperature adjustments offered no significant improvement; short vignettes showed slightly higher odds of hallucination.
links.quote: Temperature adjustments offered no significant improvement.

links.outcome: LLM elaboration on fabricated details embedded in clinical prompts (adversarial hallucination)
links.effect: Hallucination rates ranged from 50% to 82% across models and prompting methods.
links.quote: Hallucination rates ranged from 50% to 82% across models and prompting methods.

links.outcome: Elaboration of false clinical details by ungrounded LLMs
links.effect: Default-condition mean hallucination 66%; LLMs frequently generated false clinical details.
links.quote: LLMs are highly susceptible to adversarial hallucination attacks, frequently generating false clinical details that pose risks when used without safeguards.

links.outcome: Rate of hallucinated elaboration of fabricated details across multiple LLMs
links.effect: Hallucination rates 50% to 82%; mitigation prompt lowered mean from 66% to 44% (p<0.001); GPT-4o 53% to 23%.
links.quote: Prompt-based mitigation lowered overall hallucinations (mean across all models) from 66% to 44% (p<0.001).

unlisted_practices: Mitigation prompt instructing the model to avoid hallucinations reduced hallucination rate (66% to 44%)
